proposals.before: The host said: "My son is unworthy; honored by the imperial inquiry, I dare not refuse."
proposals.after: The host said: "My daughter is unworthy; honored by the imperial inquiry, I dare not refuse."
proposals.reason: In this bridal name-inquiry reply 子 means the daughter (parallel 納采 uses 女); "son" misleads.

proposals.before: The host said: "My son So-and-so is unworthy; having received the imperial inquiry, I So-and-so dare not decline."
proposals.after: The host said: "My daughter So-and-so is unworthy; having received the imperial inquiry, I So-and-so dare not decline."
proposals.reason: In this bridal name-inquiry reply 子 means the daughter; "son" misleads.

proposals.after: The envoy said: "I firmly venture to decline."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English is truncated and has a stray closing quote; restore speech form matching the Chinese.

proposals.before: The envoy said he must finally decline."
proposals.after: The envoy said: "I dare finally decline."
proposals.reason: Stray closing quote and indirect paraphrase; restore direct speech matching the Chinese.

proposals.before: The envoy stood east outside the main gate, east-facing.
proposals.after: The envoy stood west outside the main gate, east-facing.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大門外之西 is west of the outer great gate; "east outside" reverses the location.

proposals.before: The envoy stood east of the outer great gate, east-facing.
proposals.after: The envoy stood west of the outer great gate, east-facing.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大門外之西 is west of the outer great gate; literal "east" reverses the location.

decisions.reason: 厚八分 gives tablet thickness as eight fen (分 as a linear measure), not lines; the replacement restores that measure and keeps the rest faithful.

In this 問名 reply after 奉制問名, 臣某之子 names the bridal daughter; rendering 子 as "son" mis-sexes the referent in the marriage rite.
Literal field has the same bridal-context error: 子 here is the daughter under name-inquiry, not a son.
使者曰：「某敢固辭。」 is direct speech; the idiomatic line is truncated and ends with a stray quote, and the proposed wording restores the speech form.
使者曰：「敢終辭。」 is direct speech; the idiomatic paraphrase plus stray closing quote should be restored to quoted first-person decline.
大門外之西，東面立 places the envoy west outside the great gate facing east; "east outside" reverses 西.
Literal field likewise misreads 大門外之西 as east of the gate; west with east-facing stance matches the Chinese.
The trailing quote after "rose" is stray English corruption; removing it leaves an otherwise accurate rendering of 奏稱：「禮畢，興。」
Literal field has the same stray closing quote after "rose"; deleting it corrects the corruption without changing sense.
